hero.titular: Understand how you tend to think, act, relate to others and respond to what life brings, and how to turn that knowledge into more conscious decisions
hero.base: Based on Big Five/OCEAN · BFI-2 · 60 items
hero.texto: Explore five broad dimensions and fifteen facets of personality. When you finish, you will receive a personalized report that turns your results into interpretations, questions and concrete actions.
hero.rigor: A self-knowledge tool grounded in published research. It is not a diagnosis or a prediction of behavior.
hero.micro: There are no right or wrong answers. Respond thinking of how you usually act.

central.titulo: What Identify is and what you will receive
central.entradilla: Eight sections, in case you want to know what you are getting into. Open them if you feel like it; the test works just the same if you read none.

cierre.titulo: Know yourself with more depth and fewer labels
cierre.texto: Answer the 60 statements and receive a personalized reading of your five dimensions and fifteen facets.
cierre.micro: There are no right or wrong answers. Choose the option that best describes how you usually act.

explica.open_mindedness: Explores your inclination to go deep into ideas, appreciate beauty and imagine new possibilities.
explica.conscientiousness: Looks at how you structure, execute and sustain tasks, goals and commitments.
explica.extraversion: Helps understand how much you tend to seek interaction, take the initiative and keep an active pace.
explica.agreeableness: Looks at how you consider other people's needs, care for relationships and trust their intentions.
explica.negative_emotionality: Explores how readily you register worry, low mood or emotional shifts in the face of difficulties.

muestra.aria: A visual example of a report, with made-up figures

bloques.texto: Each domain is explained with its definition, the reading of your three facets and the tensions that may appear.
Questions written from your results, to take to a conversation or a notebook.
Three concrete actions, each with a signal that tells you whether it is working.

recorrido.detalle: what you can do with it

queAporta.titulo: What do you gain from taking the Identify test?
queAporta.resumen: Understand your tendencies, recognize your resources and spot the contexts where you may need a different adjustment.
queAporta.intro: Many responses show up automatically. Identify turns those tendencies into a comprehensible map so you can recognize what drives you, what may wear you down and what alternatives you can bring in depending on the situation.

tarjetas.texto: Understand your particular combination of five dimensions and fifteen facets without being reduced to a label.
Identify tendencies that can help you and the contexts where they add the most value.
Spot when a strength may stop helping you because of intensity, imbalance or context.
Observe how your tendencies can influence priorities, habits and decisions.
Understand how you tend to connect, trust, express yourself and respond to other people.
Turn the results into concrete questions and actions you can experiment with.

queAporta.destacado: The goal is not to tell you how you are in absolute terms, but to help you observe how your tendencies work and what you can do with that information.

rigor.titulo: Rigor, to understand yourself with more nuance
rigor.resumen: What the test rests on: the Big Five/OCEAN model, the structure of the BFI-2 and how far what it measures can go.
parrafos: Identify rests on the Big Five/OCEAN model and on the hierarchical structure of the BFI-2. It analyzes five broad domains and fifteen specific facets to offer a dimensional reading of personality.
This makes it possible to go beyond a label: it shows degrees, internal differences and combinations that help understand how your tendencies may express themselves in different contexts.

The results are orientative. They describe how you defined yourself when answering and should be interpreted together with your experience, your context and, when necessary, the judgment of a professional.
rigor.destacado: Science does not turn you into a label: it provides a frame to understand nuance and ask better questions.

confianza.texto: The broad domains of the Big Five model.
You answer the English original, as published by its authors.

dimensiones.resumen: The Big Five does not sort people into closed categories: we all present the five, in different degrees.
dimensiones.intro: Big Five/OCEAN does not sort people into closed categories. Everyone presents the five dimensions in different degrees, and the value of the result lies in observing how they combine.

tarjetas.texto: It represents degrees, not absolute categories.
It combines five domains with fifteen facets.
Two people with a similar domain can present different facets.
A tendency can help or hinder depending on the situation.

dimensiones.destacado: The Big Five is not out to pigeonhole you. It seeks to describe, with nuance, how you tend to operate.

cincoDimensiones.resumen: Open-Mindedness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Negative Emotionality, each with its three facets.
cincoDimensiones.intro: We all have the five dimensions. What changes is the intensity of each one and the way its facets combine.
cincoDimensiones.apunte: Anxiety, Depression and Emotional Volatility are technical names of personality scales. They do not represent clinical conditions or diagnoses.

porQueImporta.titulo: Why does knowing these dimensions matter?
porQueImporta.resumen: How they show up when you relate to others, organize yourself, manage tension and learn something new.
porQueImporta.intro: Knowing yourself does not mean labeling yourself. It means understanding which tendencies drive you, which may wear you down and which adjustments can help you respond better to each situation.

tarjetas.texto: Understand how you seek contact, voice opinions, show empathy and build trust.
Recognize how you turn intentions into actions, structure tasks and sustain commitments.
Observe how you register worry, low mood and emotional shifts when pressure rises.
Understand how you explore ideas, imagine alternatives and connect with intellectual or aesthetic experiences.
Choose different responses when your automatic tendency is not the most useful one for the situation.

informe.titulo: A personalized report: what you receive
informe.resumen: Much more than five scores: interpretation, combinations, questions and an action plan.
informe.intro: When you finish, Identify automatically generates a personalized report that explains what your results mean, how they combine and what you can do with them.
informe.apunteDominios: The domains offer the most solid view of the profile; the facets allow you to go deeper into its nuances and should be read with more caution.
informe.descubriras: What will you discover in your personalized report?
apartados: Overall summary. A headline and a general interpretation of the main patterns.
Chart of the five domains. Scores from 1 to 5 and bands in Extraversion, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness, Negative Emotionality and Open-Mindedness.
Analysis of the fifteen facets. The three facets of each domain, and which one clearly stands apart from the other two.
Interpretation of each domain. Definition, personalized reading, possible contributions, tensions and practical levers.
Profile combinations. Patterns that appear when facets are crossed and every condition of a rule is met.
Signals to watch. Combinations that come close, explained conditionally and never as current results.
At work. How those tendencies may express themselves professionally.
Powerful questions. Questions derived from your results.
Action plan. Three concrete actions, each with its follow-up indicator.
Images to remember. Three metaphors tied to the most relevant scores.
Conclusions. A synthesis of resources, adjustments and priorities.
Sources and methodology. Instrument, scale, version, references and limits.
informe.valorTitulo: The value is in what you do with the information
informe.valorTexto: The value of the report is not just in knowing a score. It is in understanding how it expresses itself in your life, which patterns are worth protecting and where a small change might prove useful.
pasos: Recognize. Put a name to tendencies you may already have sensed.
Understand. Observe how domains and facets combine.
Contextualize. Distinguish when a tendency helps and when it may hinder.
Act. Choose one concrete question or action to experiment with.
informe.apunteHipotesis: The report turns scores into hypotheses for reflection, not absolute truths.

comoLeer.titulo: A map to know yourself, not a label
comoLeer.resumen: What it measures and what it does not: the limits of what a questionnaire you answer yourself can tell you.
lista: Identify measures tendencies described by the person themselves: it reflects how you described yourself when answering.
Those tendencies are relatively stable, but not fixed, and can express themselves differently depending on context.
There are no good or bad scores. A tendency can help or hinder depending on the situation, and a mid-range score usually signals flexibility.
It is not a diagnosis or a clinical test.
It does not measure intelligence or ability, and it does not determine suitability for a job.
It does not predict exactly what you are going to do, nor does it replace the judgment of a professional.
The bands indicate your position within the questionnaire's scale. They are not a comparison with the general population: this report does not use normative percentiles.
Facets are four-item scales: they carry less weight than the domains and should be read with more caution.

baseCientifica.titulo: Get to know the scientific base of Identify
baseCientifica.resumen: Model, instrument, structure, original version and references with their DOI.

ficha.texto: Big Five/OCEAN, as a dimensional frame of personality.
The Big Five Inventory-2 (BFI-2), by Christopher J. Soto and Oliver P. John.
60 items, five domains and fifteen facets; four items per facet and twelve per domain, on a 1-to-5 scale.
The original English BFI-2, exactly as published by its authors.

Results are presented as tendencies and associations, not as diagnoses or deterministic predictions. The combinations, the questions and the action plan are IMPAUSA's own elaboration on that base, and are not part of the original instrument.

atencion.nulaTitulo: These answers don't support a reading
atencion.nulaTexto: All 60 questions are answered with the same value. The questionnaire is built so that this gives exactly the same result as answering 3 to everything — half the items are reversed on purpose, to cancel that bias — so these numbers describe nobody. It is worth taking it again, unhurried.

dominios.titulo: The five domains, facet by facet
dominios.intro: Each domain is made of three facets. Two people with the same overall score can have them distributed very differently, and that is where each profile's character lies. When a facet clearly stands apart from the other two, it is flagged in orange.

imagenes.intro: Ideas fade; images stay. These come from the scores that stray furthest from the center in your profile, and they are here to return to between sessions.

fuentesSeccion.intro: Instrument: the BFI-2, Big Five Inventory-2, in its original English version. 60 items, a 1-to-5 scale, five domains and fifteen facets. Each facet is the average of its four items; each domain, the average of its twelve. The combinations come from IMPAUSA's knowledge base on the BFI-2, built on the works listed below.
fuentesSeccion.aviso: Facets are four-item scales: they carry less weight than the domains and should be read with more caution. This report is a self-knowledge and coaching tool; it is not a clinical or selection test, and it reflects how you described yourself on the day you answered.
